Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.31% today to close at $388.90, extending a strong two-week rally of 7.8%. The gains reflect tightening global refining conditions: diesel has hit record highs due to Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and Iranian sanctions cutting off supply, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity. For a major refiner like Marathon, this creates a favorable margin environment—refineries make money by processing crude into products like diesel, and when product prices spike relative to crude costs, margins widen.

The broader geopolitical backdrop amplifies this benefit. Fresh sanctions on Iran (formalized by the EU and backed by military posturing to secure the Strait of Hormuz) and ongoing destruction of Russian refining capacity are removing competitive supply from global markets, pushing up refined product prices precisely when U.S. refiners can run at near-maximum rates to capture those higher margins.
